audit_notes: Model: shear displacement u(xi) through the coating thickness (xi = z/t, xi=0 at the tie layer/primer, xi=1 at the surface) for a graded, nearly incompressible silicone with shear modulus G = E/3 varying exponentially from G_tie at xi=0 to G_top at xi=1: d/dz(G du/dz) = 0 gives u'' = ln(E_tie/E_top) u'. Top BC is the transmitted shear stress, G_top u'(1)/t = tau. The areal compliance of the layer is C = u(1)/tau (m/Pa), and in Kendall's energy balance for a rigid base plate on a thin layer the critical shear stress is sigma_c = sqrt(2 w / C); for a uniform layer this reduces to sqrt(2 w G / t) (the Brady-Singer scaling). Analytical: u(1) = (3 tau t/E_top) (1 - exp(-beta))/beta with beta = ln 25 = 3.22, so C = 0.298*3*4e-4/2e5 = 1.79e-9 m/Pa and sigma_c = 7.5 kPa. Baseline: uniform commercial foul-release topcoat, E = 1 MPa, t = 150 um (tie modulus set equal to top modulus, beta = 0): C = 4.5e-10 m/Pa, sigma_c = 14.9 kPa. Expected gain about -50 % in release stress. Note that the gradient costs compliance: a uniform 0.2 MPa layer of 400 um would give C = 6e-9 m/Pa (sigma_c 4.1 kPa); the tie gradient trades part of the release benefit for tear resistance, which is the intended compromise. The absolute values are idealised (w = 0.05 J/m^2 without viscoelastic dissipation); measured barnacle critical removal stresses on silicones are 0.02-0.1 MPa, so only the ratio is meaningful. Parameters: all positive and physically realistic; E_top = 0.2 MPa is achievable with low-crosslink PDMS but tear strength drops to ~0.5-1 kN/m, which is the durability risk; thickness/base radius = 0.08, so the thin-layer assumption holds. Stress check: shear strain at the reference 10 kPa is gamma = 3*1e4/2e5 = 0.15, well inside the elastic range of silicone (elongation at break > 100 %). Operational loads: fender contact pressures up to MPa and cutting by debris exceed the tear resistance of the soft layer locally; this is a durability issue, not a simulation failure. Dimensionless numbers: modulus ratio 25, thickness-to-radius 0.08, grading exponent 3.22. The simulation coefficient is the areal compliance C = 1.79e-9 m/Pa (informational; equations do not use it). The model does not compute drag: the translation from release stress to time-averaged friction is left to the critic.
